newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada energy stocks hit with big selloff.
newsitem.headline: Canada energy stocks hit with big selloff.

text.p: Canadian energy stocks experienced a big selloff on Monday as a drop in world oil prices spooked investors, analysts said.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's oil and gas subindex fell 150.91 points, or 2.14 percent, to 6,895.06, with several large capitalization oil stocks taking big hits.
The drop in oils was far deeper than the broad TSE 300 index, which lost 24.69 points to end Monday's session at 6467.41. The Dow Jones Industrial Average, meanwhile, gained almost 43 points.

A sharp and unexpected drop in West Texas Intermediate oil prices over the past week to below US$19 a barrel was seen as the biggest factor in Canadian oil stock prices, Peters & Co managing director of research Wilf Gobert said.

"With the Dow hitting a new high today, this was definitely contrarian," Gobert said. "And some of the biggest name drops were the bellwether stocks." Among the big losers on Monday were Canadian Natural Resources Ltd, down 1.50 to 36, Renaissance Energy Ltd down 0.75 to 41.25, Suncor Energy Inc down 0.80 to 35.45 and Anderson Exploration Ltd off 0.50 to 18.50.
July NYMEX WTI crude closed on Monday at US$18.68 a barrel, down 11 cents. The contract has been on a decline since June 2, when it traded at US$20.98 a barrel.
Despite the oil price drop, Gobert said he was still optimistic about the industry's 1997 showing, which began with record first-quarter activity and results.
"The average price year-to-date has been above what analysts were using for their estimates, so we can afford to average US$19 or US$20 for a good part of the rest of the year," he said.
He also said natural gas prices in Canada and the United States continued to be above expections.
